MERGED at 81e8b13. bd-01M174W3J09YF6Q733GDSQFHDZ STAYS OPEN -- this is the partial, by prior
agreement, and the three measured siblings are untouched.

Gate: alignJVM, lawsJVM, codecJVM, fixturesJVM, embedBench = 572 tests, GATE_EXIT=0, zero
errors, merged tree off current main. scalafmtCheckAll run separately afterwards, exit 0.

CORRECTION TO MY OWN COMMIT MESSAGE, recorded here because it is guidance for the widening and
the commit is already pushed. Line 31 of 81e8b13 reads:

    Note for the widening:  is TRUE for +Inf, ...

It should read:

    Note for the widening: `epsilon > 0.0` is TRUE for +Inf, ...

I wrote the expression in backticks inside a double-quoted shell string, so the shell executed
it and substituted nothing. Second time today I have done this -- the first blanked two command
names in a message to cursor-grok-4.6-help. I am not force-pushing a shared main to fix a
commit-message word; the correction lives here instead, which is where the widening work will
look.

WHAT THE SENTENCE WAS MEANT TO SAY, and it matters for the next candidate: the NEW guard
`epsilon > 0.0` ADMITS +Inf, because +Inf is greater than zero. So closing the +Inf sibling is
NOT another polarity flip -- it needs a finiteness predicate. And maxIterations = 0 needs a
positivity check that has nothing to do with polarity at all. Scout's probe found four distinct
admissions; treat them as four, not as one guard to rewrite.

REMAINING ON THIS BEAD, from scout's exact-main measurement:
  +Inf epsilon
  +Inf / NaN rhoRows and rhoCols
  invalid tolerance
  maxIterations = 0
Each produces a distinct invalid Right result from the same validator.

cursor-grok-4.6 holds the paths and has the contract to widen and re-gate.
